verdict.rationale: Stagehand's own docs let you run automations on your own infrastructure without the Browserbase cloud: you can launch a local browser, attach over CDP to any running Chromium, and persist local user data. However, the pack never explicitly documents self-hosting or an open-source license, and caching is described as server-side, which implies some hosted components. missing for 10: explicit self-hosting documentation, evidence of open-source licensing or availability of the full stack (including server-side caching) without Browserbase, independent hands-on confirmation of fully self-hosted use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: There are three ways to get one: **Browserbase (`browserbase.launch`)**... **Local (`localBrowser.launch`)**... **Attach over CDP (`localBrowser.connect`)**
Attach to any Chromium browser you are already running, by URL
Stagehand creates the directory if it does not exist and leaves it in place after the browser shuts down, so the next run starts from the same cookies and local storage
